head.citation-title: Coupled influence of acidic impurities in incineration flue gas on CO2 mineralization and phase composition of steel slag-based aggregates
head.abstracts: © 2026 Elsevier B.V.Municipal solid waste incineration flue gas (MSWI) has a complex composition, in which the concentration of acidic impurity gases varies dynamically, which has a certain effect on CO2 mineralization curing. To achieve flue gas carbon capture and solid waste resource utilization, industrial solid wastes were used to prepare cold-bonded lightweight aggregates (CALAs) and their carbonation behaviors were investigated under simulated real incineration flue gas environment. Under the condition of incorporating low concentration of HCl, the carbonation process produced a synergistic promotion effect, which significantly improves the CO2 absorption efficiency to 16.7%, aggregate densification and mechanical strength, and realized net negative carbon emission; however, in the presence of medium-high concentration of HCl or SO2, the acidic gas competed for the alkaline reaction site with CO2, which inhibited the carbonation reaction, resulting in the loosening of the structure of the carbonate product and the reduction of the environmental benefits. This study demonstrated the concentration-dependent effects of HCl and SO2 in the carbonation of steel slag-based CALAs, providing an experimental basis for understanding the process of CO2 mineralization and sequestration in complex flue gas environments.

coredata.dc:description: Municipal solid waste incineration flue gas (MSWI) has a complex composition, in which the concentration of acidic impurity gases varies dynamically, which has a certain effect on CO2 mineralization curing. To achieve flue gas carbon capture and solid waste resource utilization, industrial solid wastes were used to prepare cold-bonded lightweight aggregates (CALAs) and their carbonation behaviors were investigated under simulated real incineration flue gas environment. Under the condition of incorporating low concentration of HCl, the carbonation process produced a synergistic promotion effect, which significantly improves the CO2 absorption efficiency to 16.7%, aggregate densification and mechanical strength, and realized net negative carbon emission; however, in the presence of medium-high concentration of HCl or SO2, the acidic gas competed for the alkaline reaction site with CO2, which inhibited the carbonation reaction, resulting in the loosening of the structure of the carbonate product and the reduction of the environmental benefits. This study demonstrated the concentration-dependent effects of HCl and SO2 in the carbonation of steel slag-based CALAs, providing an experimental basis for understanding the process of CO2 mineralization and sequestration in complex flue gas environments.
coredata.dc:title: Coupled influence of acidic impurities in incineration flue gas on CO2 mineralization and phase composition of steel slag-based aggregates
